title: Entropic signatures of the single-impurity Kondo state
authors: Johann Drayne, Silvia Lüscher, Will Grant, Vahid Movahed, Tim Child, Saeed Fallahi, Geoffrey C. Gardner, Michael J. Manfra, Yaakov Kleeorin, Yigal Meir, Joshua Folk
abstract: The Kondo singlet---a many-body state formed by entanglement between a localized spin and the Fermi sea---has been studied extensively through its transport signatures in quantum dots. Here we report a thermodynamic measurement of the entropy suppression associated with the formation of the Kondo singlet, using temperature-dependent charge sensing and a Maxwell relation to track the suppression of spin entropy as the first electron is added to a strongly-coupled GaAs quantum dot. Plotting $dN/dT$ against the simultaneously measured occupation $N$ reveals an asymmetric lineshape with its peak shifted to $N>1/2$---a hallmark of Kondo screening---that weakens with increasing temperature and is qualitatively reproduced by numerical renormalization group (NRG) calculations, with a small but persistent offset to lower occupation relative to the theory. An independent measurement of conductance versus occupation on the same device provides a test of these quantities through the mixed-valence crossover and matches NRG within experimental uncertainty.
summary: The authors report on the measurement of entropic signatures and conductance characteristics associated with the formation of the Kondo singlet state in a quantum dot. By analyzing temperature-dependent charge sensing and direct conductance measurements, they confirm the predicted asymmetric spectral features characteristic of Kondo screening. The quantitative agreement between these experimental results and NRG theory strongly validates the theoretical understanding of correlated electron physics in nanoscale devices.
main_problem: To measure the entropy suppression associated with the formation of the Kondo singlet state in a quantum dot.
main_result: The measured entropy signature ($dN/dT$) and conductance peak shift both exhibit an asymmetric lineshape peaking at $N>1/2$, which is confirmed by independent measurements and matches theoretical predictions from NRG calculations.
method: Entropy change is extracted using a Maxwell relation applied to temperature-dependent charge sensing ($\Delta I_{CS} \propto dN/dT$), complemented by direct conductance ($G$) measurements.
model_or_system: The system is a single impurity coupled to leads, realized in a GaAs quantum dot exhibiting Kondo screening below the characteristic temperature $T_K$. Theoretical modeling relies heavily on Numerical Renormalization Group (NRG) calculations.
key_observables: $dN/dT$ vs. occupation $N$; Conductance $G$ vs. occupation $N$; Zero-Bias Anomaly (ZBA) splitting in differential conductance ($dI/dV$).
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K$), Hybridization ($\Gamma$), Temperature ($T$), Occupation number ($N$).
main_assumptions: The entropy measurement relies on the Maxwell relation, and parameter fitting requires assuming consistency between measurements derived from charge sensing and conductance.
figures_summary: Figures compare measured $dN/dT$ vs. $N$ (showing peak shift) and $G$ vs. $N$ against NRG theory across various temperatures; later figures show ZBA splitting in differential conductance as a function of magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents multiple measurements on the same system, first establishing the entropy signature ($dN/dT$), then providing independent confirmation using conductance ($G(N)$), and finally verifying results on a second device using both techniques alongside magnetic field dependence studies.
why_interesting: This work provides highly quantitative experimental verification of fundamental many-body physics (the Kondo effect) by measuring thermodynamic quantities like entropy, which is crucial for understanding quantum impurity models in mesoscopic systems.
